passages.text: Now concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to Him, we ask you, brothers, not to be easily disconcerted or alarmed by any spirit or message or letter seeming to be from us, alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers.
He calls them brothers.
He speaks about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
He also speaks about our gathering together to Jesus.
Paul and his companions ask the believers for something.
They ask the believers not to be easily shaken in mind.
They ask the believers not to be alarmed.
No spirit should disturb them.
No message should disturb them.
No letter should disturb them.
Some letters may seem to come from Paul and his companions.
Some messages may claim that the Day of the Lord has already come.
Paul tells the believers not to believe these claims.
passages.original: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί ὑπὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτόν εἰς τὸ μὴ ταχέως σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς μηδὲ θροεῖσθαι μήτε διὰ πνεύματος μήτε διὰ λόγου μήτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι’ ἡμῶν ὡς ὅτι ἐνέστηκεν ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: Let no one deceive you in any way, for it will not come until the rebellion occurs and the man of lawlessness—the son of destruction—is revealed.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
He warns them about the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ.
He says, "Do not let anyone deceive you in any way."
The Day of the Lord will not come yet.
First, the rebellion must happen.
Then, the man of lawlessness will be revealed.
This man is also called the son of destruction.
passages.original: μή τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατήσῃ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας

passages.text: He will oppose and exalt himself above every so-called god or object of worship. So he will seat himself in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God.
passages.sermon:
The man of lawlessness will appear.
He will oppose every so-called god.
He will exalt himself above every object of worship.
He will enter the temple of God.
He will sit in the temple.
He will claim that he is God.
passages.original: ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον Θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καθίσαι ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἔστιν Θεός

passages.text: Do you not remember that I told you these things while I was still with you?
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul spoke to the Thessalonian believers.
Paul told them important things before.
Paul was with them when he spoke these things.
Paul asks if they remember what he told them.
passages.original: Οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ἔτι ὢν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταῦτα ἔλεγον ὑμῖν

passages.text: And you know what is now restraining him, so that he may be revealed at the proper time.
passages.sermon: You know what restrains the lawless one now.\r\nThis restraint keeps him hidden.\r\nHe will be revealed at the time appointed for him.
passages.original: καὶ νῦν τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε εἰς τὸ ἀποκαλυφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἑαυτοῦ καιρῷ

passages.text: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work, but the one who now restrains it will continue until he is taken out of the way.
passages.sermon:
The mystery of lawlessness is already at work.
Someone is now restraining this lawlessness.
This restrainer will continue to hold it back.
He will restrain it until he is taken out of the way.
passages.original: τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται

passages.text: And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of His mouth and annihilate by the majesty of His arrival.
passages.sermon:
The lawless one will appear.
The Lord Jesus will destroy the lawless one.
Jesus will use the breath of His mouth to slay him.
Jesus will bring the lawless one to nothing by the majesty of His coming.
passages.original: καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος ὃν ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀνελεῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The coming of the lawless one will be accompanied by the working of Satan, with every kind of power, sign, and false wonder, and with every wicked deception directed against those who are perishing, because they refused the love of the truth that would have saved them.
passages.sermon:
The lawless one will come.
Satan will empower his coming.
Satan will give him all kinds of power.
He will perform signs.
He will perform wonders that are false.
He will use every kind of wicked deception.
He will deceive those who are perishing.
These people are perishing because they refused to love the truth.
The truth could have saved them.
They did not accept it.
passages.original: οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ’ ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασιν ψεύδους καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις ἀνθ’ ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς

passages.text: For this reason God will send them a powerful delusion so that they believe the lie, in order that judgment may come upon all who have disbelieved the truth and delighted in wickedness.
passages.sermon:
God acts with purpose.
God will send a powerful delusion to certain people.
These people will believe a lie.
God does this for a reason.
God wants judgment to come upon all who have not believed the truth.
These people have chosen to delight in wickedness.
passages.original: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμπει αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει ἵνα κριθῶσιν πάντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀλλὰ εὐδοκήσαντες τῇ ἀδικίᾳ

passages.text: But we should always thank God for you, brothers who are loved by the Lord, because God has chosen you from the beginning to be saved by the sanctification of the Spirit and by faith in the truth.
passages.sermon:
We should always thank God for you.
You are brothers.
The Lord loves you.
God chose you from the beginning.
God chose you to be saved.
God saves you through the sanctification of the Spirit.
God saves you through faith in the truth.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ ὀφείλομεν εὐχαριστεῖν τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν ἀδελφοὶ ἠγαπημένοι ὑπὸ Κυρίου ὅτι εἵλατο ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ἀπ᾽‿ ἀρχῆς εἰς σωτηρίαν ἐν ἁγιασμῷ Πνεύματος καὶ πίστει ἀληθείας

passages.text: To this He called you through our gospel, so that you may share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon: God called you.\r\nHe called you through our gospel.\r\nHe called you so that you may share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ὑμᾶς διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἡμῶν εἰς περιποίησιν δόξης τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Therefore, brothers, stand firm and cling to the traditions we taught you, whether by speech or by letter.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
He calls them brothers.
He urges them to stand firm.
He tells them to hold on to the traditions.
Paul and his companions taught these traditions.
They taught them by speaking.
They also taught them by writing letters.
passages.original: Ἄρα οὖν ἀδελφοί στήκετε καὶ κρατεῖτε τὰς παραδόσεις ἃς ἐδιδάχθητε εἴτε διὰ λόγου εἴτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ἡμῶν

passages.text: Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself and God our Father, who by grace has loved us and given us eternal comfort and good hope, encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good word and deed.
passages.sermon:
Our Lord Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
God is our Father.
God our Father has loved us.
God has given us eternal comfort.
God has given us good hope by His grace.
May Jesus Christ and God our Father encourage your hearts.
May they strengthen you in every good word.
May they strengthen you in every good deed.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ὁ Πατὴρ ἡμῶν ὁ ἀγαπήσας ἡμᾶς καὶ δοὺς παράκλησιν αἰωνίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα ἀγαθὴν ἐν χάριτι παρακαλέσαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας καὶ στηρίξαι ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἀγαθῷ
